slides.title: Considerations for Happy Eyeballs Error Reporting

polls.text: I have read a recent version of the HEv3 draft

chat.author: Tim Chown
chat.text: what changed from -04 to -05 is here: https://author-tools.ietf.org/iddiff?url2=draft-ietf-happy-happyeyeballs-v3-05

chat.author: Tim Chown
chat.text: /wave

chat.author: Erik Nygren
chat.text:
Thumbs up to keep-rather-than-cancel but with a recommendation to only use if it planning to use it within some reasonable timeframe (eg, a minute).  (Would this also help/apply for transitioning to IPv6 if IPv4 wins the race with IPv6 as a fast follow?)
I think it's mostly the "never used" which could be odd.  I guess this could cause some server-side telemetry issues --- this certainly happens all the time routinely but is often a symptom of something broken (eg, PMTUD failing sometimes looks similar).

chat.author: Eric Kinnear
chat.text: +1 for considering this for IPv6 stragglers as well

chat.author: Erik Nygren
chat.text: But I think the fundamental aspect is that connection establishment performance is not necessarily indicative of ongoing connection performance, so being able to transition to stragglers would be good as an option.

chat.author: Erik Nygren
chat.text: I did a fresh read of -04 or -03 which I failed to actually send notes on, but I had some of the same take-away as Ben of it being maybe worth looking at from a fresh read.  I will do a read of this latest version and will also take since that may have improved since.

chat.author: Chris Box
chat.text: Lars may know the answer: would you have statistically valid data for P99.9?

chat.author: Chris Box
chat.text: Asking because the benefit at P99 is 400ms; at P99.9 it could be greater than 1s

chat.author: Erik Nygren
chat.text: Was this first contentful paint controlled for "has H3"?   (ie, is this looking at the family of H3-capable hostnames?)

chat.author: Erik Nygren
chat.text: (eg, controlling those sorts of things is hard but important here.  for example it makes the "is IPv6 faster?" impossible to measure from the server side alone since the IPv4-only vs dualstack client populations have strong correlations with factors that end up being dominant (eg, like "mobile is usually dualstacked" and "enterprise networks are usually IPv4 only")

chat.author: Erik Nygren
chat.text: +1 to Ben on both points/concerns.

chat.author: Chris Box
chat.text: Thanks Max! I thought it would be a valuable improvement for the user. When do you estimate you'll have collected enough data to be able to have confidence in the value?

chat.author: Erik Nygren
chat.text: (I once found a buggy "managed client" implementation that filtered AAAA records for everything ending in .com due to a typo in config -- that was exciting to chase down.)

chat.author: Dave Plonka
chat.text: It's worth recalling Mirja's point that (a) we want to fix problems and (b) HE[v3] has the potential to hide problems. To me, this makes it worthwhile considering how to expose what HE[v3] learned, that is so close to determining user experience.

chat.author: Lars Eggert
chat.text: Who is the "we" here

chat.author: Lars Eggert
chat.text: Servers?

chat.author: Dave Plonka
chat.text: IETF practices I guess is the "we" I meant.

chat.author: Stephen Farrell
chat.text: how might efficacy of any such reporting be established before taking on the pricacy leak? I don't know how to answer that, so tend to agree with Lars that this is maybe better not done.

chat.author: Lars Eggert
chat.text:
So Mozilla makes a lot of data available, see https://glam.telemetry.mozilla.org/
But that is VERY different than sending request-specific data for specific HE3 decisions to somewhere in the network, which is I think what this I-D is about

chat.author: Dave Plonka
chat.text: I agree (w/Stephen, Lars) there isn't a short path to justifying telemetry.

chat.author: Daniel Gillmor
chat.text: the telemetry suggestions also make me very nervous

chat.author: Daniel Gillmor
chat.text: i think Philipp's mic might be hot, and the cause of the noise.  Philipp can you mute when you're not speaking?

chat.author: Tim Chown
chat.text: aha

chat.author: Daniel Gillmor
chat.text: +1 Tommy

chat.author: Dave Plonka
chat.text: Tommy's point about HE-induced behaviors being passively measured is a good one. However, subtle variations in HE implementation make it hard to deeply understand that in an external analyzer (think wireshark.) It seems attractive to consider if the HE implementation can expose what its choosing to do.

chat.author: Erik Nygren
chat.text:
I'm not sure enough of that brokenness will be visible deep enough in the network.  eg, if you have a broken CPE that's not going to show you stuff. 
Also that really requires better understanding things than networks may be able to see -- eg, for a given CDN any given set of IPs is going to have a wide mix of dual-stack and IPv4-only things using those IPs.

chat.author: Jen Linkova
chat.text: IF you have CPEs - how can you get the data from enpoints? I do not want my laptop tp report things to my ISP

chat.text: calling Dave Plonka to do some tests...

chat.author: Erik Nygren
chat.text: +1 to Ben's "you can't reasonably do this passively".  This is hard enough to do in the endpoints with tcpdumps knowing the IP correlations.

chat.author: Erik Nygren
chat.text: Being able to send  data up to servers participating seems like something we could do reasonably, and even that could really help.
